nodes.label: Institutions
nodes.rationale: Implemented in revision 0014. A tenant was one college. A university that shares a few labs and a visiting professor needs a level inside the tenant, because a separate tenant cannot share a room or a person.

nodes.label: Tenant organization institution department
nodes.rationale: Tenant is the customer and the isolation boundary. Organization is exactly one row. Institution is the college, school or campus and the accreditation unit. Department remains the HOD scope. A standalone college is one organization and one institution and behaves exactly as before. Nothing here requires the tenant registry; it works in single-database mode too.

nodes.label: Institution ownership through departments
nodes.rationale: An institution owns courses, subjects, students, allocations, timetable slots, lecture sessions and attendance through the department of the course. High-volume tables never get an institution_id; they inherit through the course. Rooms are anchored directly. Classes, divisions, academic years, semesters, shifts, holidays, roles, branding and notification settings stay organization-wide on purpose, as vocabularies or policy. Per-institution overrides are the obvious next step and are not in this revision.

nodes.label: Request scope
nodes.rationale: core/scope.py resolves a Scope per request. Super Admin is organization-wide. Everyone else sees their memberships. Reads of a row outside the scope answer not found, so the id is not confirmed. Writes on a shared row the caller can see but does not own answer 403. The scope is in addition to permissions. The session stores only the chosen institution_id; the visible list is read on each request, so a membership change applies without a new sign-in.

nodes.label: One-college short-circuit
nodes.rationale: While the tenant has at most one active institution, multiple is false, every predicate is 1=1 and allows is always true, so a one-college install runs exactly the pre-0014 queries. A staff user with no membership is placed in the institution of their department, else the first institution. The switcher, institution field and sharing controls appear only when more than one institution is active.

nodes.label: Room and faculty sharing
nodes.rationale: A shared resource is one row with a policy, never a copy. private is the owning institution, listed adds resource_shares, and organization is every institution of the tenant. Both solvers load rooms through that predicate, so one joint run over two colleges gives each its own pool and a shared elective the intersection. Clash rules do not change: timetable already holds every slot of the tenant, so a shared lab booked by one college is busy for another with no extra ledger. Only the owner edits sharing. Deleting a row other institutions use is refused.

nodes.label: Institution memberships
nodes.rationale: A user may belong to several institutions with different roles. users.role and users.department_id stay the primary identity. The 0014 backfill puts every non-student into institution 1, and a new teacher joins the institution of their department. Other memberships are added with SQL for now; the user editor has no Institutions field yet. The last active institution cannot be deactivated.

nodes.label: Institution follow-ups
nodes.rationale: Not in revision 0014: per-institution overrides of calendar, attendance policy, branding and notifications; cross-institution student enrolment; an organization dashboard; sharing of lab batch groups or subjects; and scoping of reports, accreditation exports, invitations, the user list and the public API.
